title: Liczba mnoga
note: NON-VIRILE ONLY. Four noun endings (-y / -i after k,g / -e soft / -a neuter) plus one adjective rule (-e always). The k/g -> -i branch is the payoff of a1_gen_ki ('Polish never writes y after k or g') and is called out as the same fact doing a second job — intro slide 2 says so in words, and the explains on banki/apteki/parki repeat it. Accusative plural = Nominative plural for every non-virile noun: taught explicitly on intro slide 6 and drilled in use_items (Mam nowe książki, Tata czytał gazety). FENCED, appear nowhere in this file: the suppletive/irregular plurals of dziecko, oko, ucho, ręka, człowiek and the plural-only money word; every virile (male-person) plural; and pokój, whose stem vowel shifts. See NIGHT-BATCH-3 for the explicit list. Past tense stays SINGULAR here — plural past (-li/-ły) is a2_past_plural, which lands next; plural nouns therefore appear as objects of a singular-subject past verb, or as subjects of present-tense są. Numerals excluded (a2_numbers_gen). No negation over a plural object — that would demand the genitive plural, which is a2_gen_pl.

intro.title: Mianownik liczby mnogiej — the plural: -y
intro.body:
The plural is a form of the noun, and this unit builds it in the nominative — the case a noun takes as the subject of a sentence, and its dictionary form.

Most nouns take -y. A noun ending in a consonant adds it: sklep → sklepy. A noun ending in -a swaps that -a for -y: gazeta → gazety.

This is the main rule; the three slides that follow are its exceptions.

One more form: to jest (this is) becomes to są in the plural.
intro.body_pl: Większość rzeczowników: -y. sklep → sklepy, gazeta → gazety. To jest → to są.

intro.title: After k and g: -i, never -y
intro.body:
You already know this one. When you learned the genitive, a single spelling fact finished the rule: Polish never writes y after k or g. That is why it was apteki and książki, never apteky.

It is the same fact here, doing a second job. A word whose stem ends in k or g takes -i in the plural, for exactly the same reason:

bank → banki · park → parki · książka → książki

Nothing new to learn. One fact, two rules.
intro.body_pl: Po k i g nigdy nie piszemy y — więc w liczbie mnogiej -i: bank → banki, książka → książki.

intro.title: A small group takes -e
intro.body:
A few words end in a soft sound — written -l, -cz, -c or -j. These take -e.

There are not many of them at this level, so learn these three whole and you have the group:

hotel → hotele · klucz → klucze · lekcja → lekcje

Watch lekcja. It ends in -a, so you would expect -y. But the sound in front of the -a is the soft -j-, and after a soft sound the ending is -e.
intro.body_pl: Miękkie zakończenia biorą -e: hotel → hotele, klucz → klucze, lekcja → lekcje.

intro.title: Neuter words take -a
intro.body:
Neuter nouns — the ones ending in -o — swap the -o for -a.

This one looks odd at first, because -a is also how a feminine singular word ends: kawa, gazeta. But on a word that ended in -o, the -a can only mean more than one.
intro.body_pl: Rodzaj nijaki: -o → -a. piwo → piwa, miasto → miasta.

intro.title: Adjectives: always -e
intro.body:
The nouns have four endings. The adjectives have one.

Whatever the noun is — masculine, feminine or neuter — the adjective in front of it takes -e. There is nothing to choose:

dobre domy · małe koty · nowe książki · duże miasta

A neuter noun already had -e in the singular (duże miasto), so on those nothing changes at all.
intro.body_pl: Przymiotnik w liczbie mnogiej zawsze -e: dobre domy, małe koty, nowe książki, duże miasta.

intro.title: Biernik = mianownik (w liczbie mnogiej)
intro.body:
In the singular, a noun changes when it becomes the object of a verb — the accusative: kawa → Mam kawę, książka → Mam książkę.

In the plural it does not. The form you have just learned does both jobs unchanged:

Książki są nowe. — The books are new. (subject · nominative)
Mam nowe książki. — I have new books. (object · accusative)

For these nouns the accusative plural and the nominative plural are the same form. That is one fewer ending to learn, and it holds for every noun in this unit.
intro.body_pl: W liczbie mnogiej biernik = mianownik: Książki są nowe. Mam nowe książki.

quiz.explain: The stem ends in k, and Polish never writes y after k or g — the same fact that gave you apteki instead of apteky. So the plural ending has to be -i.
k refuses y, so the ending is -i. You met this word doing exactly the same thing in the genitive — one fact, two jobs.
parky is not a possible Polish spelling. After k the vowel is written i, never y.
Words ending in -o are neuter, and neuter swaps the -o for -a. The -y ending belongs to the masculine and feminine words.
hotel ends in a soft -l, and soft endings take -e. It is a small group — hotel, klucz, lekcja — worth learning whole.
Adjectives have only one plural ending. Whatever the noun is, the adjective takes -e — so there is no gender choice left to make here.
The word is the object, but in the plural the object form is the same as the subject form. Nothing extra happens to it — unlike the singular, where kawa became kawę.

type_items.explain: A word ending in -a does not keep it. The -a is swapped for the plural -y, not added to.
Polish never writes y after k or g — the rule you already used for apteki. So this one can only end -i.
Same k, same rule, same ending you wrote in the genitive. The spelling fact does not care which case you are in.
Soft ending, so -e. If you wrote hotely you were reaching for the main rule; this is one of the small group that sits outside it.
It ends in -a, so -y looks right — but the sound in front of the -a is soft, and a soft sound always pulls -e.
There is no gender to work out. Every adjective in front of a plural noun ends -e.

use_items.explain: In the singular this would have been Mam nową książkę — both words changed. In the plural neither does: the object form and the subject form are the same word.
gazety is the object here, and it is still the plain plural — nothing is added to it. In the singular an object always changed shape: Mam kawę, never Mam kawa.
